sections.title: Text: is the model. Quotes are the website.
sections.lede: Auto-quotes only work on novelai.net. Everywhere else you must send Text: yourself.
sections.body:
ght901 (Anlatan Team / Web Dev) spent a long evening cleaning up Text: folklore. The only way the model understands in-image text is through a `Text:` / `text:` block. Turning `"quoted strings"` into `Text:` is a **frontend UI** feature — other frontends (Dreamscape included, until they implement it) do not get that helper for free. Unicode quotes work for the novelai.net helper. If you write `Text:` by hand, the model tries to draw **exactly** what follows; if you also wrap quotes in the payload, the pixels get quotes. And the big myth-kill: **all casings of `text:` are treated the same by the model** — older anecdotes about lowercase `text:` confusing the encoder are out.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler / karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on (No-text sub-toggle off), rescale 0. Prompt base: `1girl, outdoors, holding a sign, looking at viewer`. A: let the UI lift `"hello world"` from the speaker box. B: manual last line `Text: hello world` with no quotes. C: `Text: "hello world"` with quotes in the payload. Look for missing text vs exact letters vs drawn quotation marks.

**Call to action.** If you are on Studio/MCP, confirm whether your path auto-lifts quotes. If it does not, always emit `Text:` yourself. save_memory the A/B/C trio.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: The turning quotes into `text:` is a frontend UI thing. It won't work on other frontends unless they also implement that feature. The only way the model understands text is through `text:`

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: If you use `text:` the text the model will try to output will be exactly what follows. If you add quotes, the model will add quotes to the image

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: All casings if `text:` are treated the same by the model

sections.title: Retune Strength. V5 is not V4.5 with a new coat.
sections.lede: img2img is sampling physics, not a trained dial. Your old Strength is lying to you.
sections.body:
.mahouko was blunt: staff cannot "change how img2img works," because it is a consequence of how sampling works — not a feature they train into the model. The practical line for everyone who ported a V4.5 workflow: **find a different Strength on V5**. Pair that with luna's earlier meter note (img2img drain follows Strength, not Noise) and you get both the prompting and the battery story in one place.

**Try this.** Take one V4.5 keeper you used to img2img at Strength 0.5. Same seed family on V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, QT on, rescale 0. Sweep Strength 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.65. Look for composition lock vs mush. Keep the rung that matches your old intent.

**Call to action.** Do not open a "V5 img2img is broken" thread until you have three Strengths on the same seed. save_memory the rung that ports.

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: most likely you need to find a different img2img strength for v5 than the one you were using on v4.5

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: img2img is not a feature that we train into the model, it’s a consequence of how sampling works.

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: we can’t change how img2img works

sections.title: Euler when you have the budget. 2S costs twice.
sections.lede: Multistep can make you chase higher step counts for the wrong reason. Read the UI step count carefully on 2S/SDE.
sections.body:
.mahouko's sampler thread this weekend is the one to tape above the desk. Multistep sampling is often harmful because the second derivative is weak — high step counts can be compensating for multistep error at large step sizes. With a high step budget, prefer more **Euler** steps. For second-order single-step samplers (DPM++ 2S Ancestral, DPM++ SDE), each UI "step" costs **two** model invocations, so you only get half as many diffusion steps as Euler at the same number. Small images have fewer octaves of signal: budget **at least ~14 steps** if you want a pure-noise step, or the image invents contrast to average mean colour to 0. The paper graph in-thread is context — staff commentary is the recipe.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, guidance 5, QT on, rescale 0, normal_square. A: Euler 28. B: DPM++ 2S Ancestral 28 (UI). C: Euler 14 on a small 640×640 crop. Compare fidelity vs battery. If B looks "expensive for what you got," you felt the 2× invocation tax.

**Call to action.** Default stays Euler. Only switch samplers with a same-seed reason. save_memory if 14-vs-28 on small res surprises you.

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: multistep sampling is harmful because the second derivative is crap

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: if you have a high step budget you can just do more Euler steps

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: you should do at least 14 if you want it to budget a pure-noise step. otherwise your image will add spurious regions of contrast to make the mean colour average out to 0

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: for second-order single-step samplers (DPM++ 2S Ancestral, DPM++ SDE): each step costs twice as much (you have to invoke the model twice to compute velocity then acceleration). so for those samplers "steps" in the UI refers to the number of times you invoke the model.

sections.title: 0.001 is the real CFG0. Guidance 0 is a low-complexity toy.
sections.lede: The UI still maps 0→1. Staff pointed at 0.001. Community found guidance 0 fun on simple prompts.
sections.body:
Prior STAFF math still stands: NAI UI overrides CFG 0 to CFG 1. .mahouko's tip this window: **0.001** shows what CFG0 is actually meant to look like under their sampling shenanigans. sergalaluminum then posted low-complexity gens at guidance **0** that behave like Variety+ on steroids — style swings hard per seed while mostly adhering to the prompt with acceptable anatomy. That community half is **ANECDOTE**, not a dense-prompt default. Keep collapse-then-lower-CFG as the main staff recipe; treat near-zero as a deliberate experiment.

**Try this.** Simple prompt only: `1girl, white fur, anthro, wolf, standing, black background, flat color`. V5 Full, Euler, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Same seed at guidance 5 / 1 / 0.001 / 0. Look for diversity vs collapse. Do **not** run this on a novel-length prompt.

**Call to action.** One simple prompt. Four guidances. save_memory only if 0.001 teaches you something 0 did not.

excerpts.text: 0.001 shows you what CFG0 is actually meant to look like, were it not for our shenanigans

excerpts.speaker: sergalaluminum
excerpts.text: woah, turns out for low-complexity gens, **0** prompt guidance is actually kinda viable, and gives big Variety+ on steroids vibes / the style and everything else changes wildly with every gen, while staying kinda adhered to the prompt with mostly acceptable anatomy

sections.title: -1::overexposure:: as a text crispener?
sections.lede: One user's A/B says negative overexposure helps in-image text. Needs repeats.
sections.body:
runtime_m1 noticed `-1::overexposure::` cleaned text on V4.5 and ran a quick V5 A/B (control vs -1). Past about -2 the side effects get loud. This is a single-user ladder — **ANECDOTE** until someone else reproduces it on a different seed and font style. Do not promote to CONSENSUS or optimiser defaults yet.

**Try this.** Prompt: `1girl, holding a sign, Text: hello world, soft daylight`. UC light. V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on (No-text off), rescale 0. Same seed A: no overexposure tag. B: add `-1::overexposure::` to the base prompt. Compare letter sharpness vs washed whites.

**Call to action.** Two gens. If B wins on your font, save_memory with seed + screenshot. If not, leave it as a zine curiosity.

sections.title: Minimal UC still works. Watch for scanlines.
sections.lede: Shambibble's thin UC remains a community favorite. scanlines in UC may not kill vertical lines.
sections.body:
sergalaluminum is still running Shambibble's minimal V5 UC: `lowres, adversarial noise, jpeg artifacts, worst quality, very displeasing`. Low style implication, good hygiene — but some settings grow subtle vertical scan lines, and putting `scanlines` in UC did not clear them for that user. Keep as ANECDOTE reinforcement of the existing adversarial_noise story, not a new CONSENSUS preset.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Prompt: `1girl, cafe, soft daylight, looking at viewer`. UC A: official Light. UC B: the minimal five-tag string above. Look for style drift and any vertical lines.

**Call to action.** If B is cleaner for your style, save_memory. If scanlines appear, try a different sampler/res before blaming the UC.

sections.title: Bucket-drop the lookalikes.
sections.lede: When two characters share a face, a handful of unique tags can tip the tokenizer.
sections.body:
shambibble's tip: if your character is being confused with another, bucket-drop a few tags specific to that character — e.g. `brown hair, blue visor, bare arms` was enough for "Lesser Pokemon Girl." Training is there; the tokenizer is just noisy. ANECDOTE, but it pairs cleanly with collapse-distribution STAFF advice.

**Try this.** Pick a lookalike pair you always lose. Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps. A: bare character tag. B: character tag + 3–5 unique identity tags. Prefer tags that are true on the target and false on the impostor.

**Call to action.** One confused OC. Two gens. Board it only if B sticks across three seeds.

excerpts.text: if your character is being confused with another one you can bucket drop it with a handful of tags specific to that character, i think "brown hair, blue visor, bare arms" was enough for Lesser Pokemon Girl. the training is all there the tokenizer is just inherently going to be lo

sections.title: Panties aside ≠ waistband pull.
sections.lede: Unofficial tip: the model ties the two phrases. UC the waistband wording.
sections.body:
amber_delphox on unofficial nai-image-gen-discussion: `pulling panties aside` often equals `pulling on waist band`. Putting the waistband phrasing in the negative removes the yanking motion and leaves the garment aside. Keep **[UNOFFICIAL]** — one speaker, NSFW guild.

**Try this.** NSFW 2+, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Prompt: `1girl, panties, pulling panties aside, standing`. UC A: empty. UC B: `pulling on waistband, tugging waistband`. Same seed.

**Call to action.** Grim lab only. save_memory if B freezes the aside pose without the yank.

excerpts.speaker: amber_delphox
excerpts.text: see thing is pulling panties aside = pulling on waist band.  adding the latter to negative removes the act of pulling them to the side and just puts it there.

sections.title: Five battery-aware experiments for the week.
sections.lede: Pick two. Free/Opus only. Stop before the meter cries.
sections.body:
Monday sheet lab board — concrete, lowercase, same-seed friendly:

1. **Text: A/B/C** — UI quotes vs manual `Text:` vs quoted payload (see Text: feature).
2. **img2img Strength sweep** — 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.65 on one V4.5 port.
3. **Euler 28 vs 2S 28** — feel the 2× invocation tax.
4. **CFG 5 / 0.001 / 0** on a *simple* prompt only.
5. **`-1::overexposure::`** on a sign/speech still.

Settings default unless noted: V5 Full, Euler / karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Guren: dedicated workspace, Opus/free only, save_memory when pixels settle. Ivory: fold Text:/img2img notes into Studio cohesion. Chiyo: webapp e3f74dd + any UI deltas → Rook.

**Try this.** Literally the list above. Two is enough. Five is a feast day.

**Call to action.** Reply in-cellar with seed + which rung won. No Discord screenshots required — Hoshino already has the excerpts.
